$comment: WHAT: Deterministic enforcement for the rules in AGENTS.md.
WHY:  AGENTS.md is delivered to the model as a user message, not as system config.
The model judges relevance and may skip rules it deems unrelated to the task.
That is by design, not a bug. Anything that must happen 100% of the time
belongs here, at the shell level, where the model has no vote.
Rule of thumb: AGENTS.md is what the agent must KNOW. Hooks are what must
HAPPEN regardless of what it knows.
CONSUMED BY: Claude Code. Codex and Cursor read AGENTS.md but not this file —
the same checks run in CI, so enforcement is identical for every agent.

hooks.$comment: Blocks edits to vendor/, to golden fixtures without an explicit flag, and blocks any write while on the main branch.

hooks.command: uv run ruff format $CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS && uv run ruff check --fix $CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS
hooks.$comment: Formatting and lint are mechanical. They never belong in AGENTS.md — they cost instruction budget and the model applies them inconsistently. Here they are certain.
The 200-line and 15-file caps are checked immediately after every write, so the agent sees the violation on the turn it created it rather than at commit time.
Layering, docstrings and naming. Same reasoning: immediate feedback beats a CI failure twenty minutes later.

Runs at the end of every session. Reminds — and records — whether docs/CODEBASE.md was updated to match the changes made, and whether `just verify` was run. Writes a session record to docs/plans/ so the next session (or the next developer) can see what was and was not validated.

$enforcement_map.$comment: Every rule in AGENTS.md maps to exactly one enforcement mechanism. A rule with no mechanism is advisory and must be tagged as such in AGENTS.md.
$enforcement_map.plan before editing resolve/ or label/: ADVISORY ONLY — human review in PR
